The structure of Ca16N12 (reduced formula Ca4N3) crystallizes in the monoclinic space group C2/m (No. 119), with 28 atoms per unit cell distributed over six independent Wyckoff orbits. Geometry-derived analysis identifies octahedral N environments with six Ca neighbors (distances 2.47–2.58 Å) and two-coordinate N environments with two Ca neighbors. Ca centers show four- or five-coordinate N environments. Validated polyhedron contacts reveal corner- and edge-sharing between octahedral N polyhedra and corner-sharing between octahedral and five-vertex Ca polyhedra, forming a three-dimensional periodic connectivity network.
